subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw change its Codex app-server auth bridge to avoid forced OAuth refresh during `account/chatgptAuthTokens/refresh`, or should this wait for an upstream Codex timeout/configuration change?
rationale: The source-level root cause crosses OpenClaw bridge semantics and upstream Codex's external-auth RPC timeout, and the current open candidate shows that cached-token reuse can conflict with explicit 401 recovery semantics.

options.title: Use reason-aware bridge behavior
options.body: Teach the bridge to return cached usable tokens only for safe non-401/proactive paths, while preserving real provider refresh for Unauthorized callbacks and proving both cases live.

options.title: Coordinate upstream timeout configurability
options.body: Keep OpenClaw behavior unchanged and rely on Codex exposing a longer or configurable external-auth refresh timeout before closing this issue.

options.title: Fold into broader auth incidents
options.body: Track this under the wider auth-profile quarantine/status work, accepting that this specific 10-second callback report remains open until a broader design lands.

recommendation.title: Use reason-aware bridge behavior
recommendation.body: Teach the bridge to return cached usable tokens only for safe non-401/proactive paths, while preserving real provider refresh for Unauthorized callbacks and proving both cases live.

likelyOwner.reason: The older feature history most directly ties this path to canonical Codex OAuth routing and auth hardening work rather than the recent packaging re-add.
